texts.W1: Okay, so suppose y cubed minus eight equals zero. Then take the square root of minus one and call it i. Now look at one over n as n grows, and finally at three x plus two y.
texts.S1: Okay, so suppose y^3 - 8 = 0. Then take sqrt(-1) and call it i. Now look at 1/n as n grows, and finally at 3x + 2y.
texts.W2: Right, so we had two to the power of ten yesterday. Today we multiply, alpha times beta, then divide, z over four, and we subtract, seven minus three, and we are done.
texts.S2: Right, so we had 2^10 yesterday. Today we multiply, α × β, then divide, z/4, and we subtract, 7 - 3, and we are done.
texts.N0: Okay, so, um, right, and then, well, anyway.
texts.M1a: Okay, so suppose y cubed minus 8 equals 0. Then take the square root of minus 1 and call it i. Now look at 1 over n as n grows, and finally at 3 x plus 2 y.
texts.M1b: Right, so we had 2 to the power of 10 yesterday. Today we multiply, alpha times beta, then divide, z over 4, and we subtract, 7 minus 3, and we are done.
texts.M2a: Okay, so suppose y^three - eight = zero. Then take sqrt(-one) and call it i. Now look at one/n as n grows, and finally at three x + two y.
texts.M2b: Right, so we had two^ten yesterday. Today we multiply, α × β, then divide, z/four, and we subtract, seven - three, and we are done.
